To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
methyl jasmonate induces chilling tolerance of rice plants by enhancing the biosynthesis of polyamines, especially putrescine.
MeJA induces chilling tolerance in rice seedlings and that the induction of chilling resistance is associated with an increase in the level of polyamines.
MeJA induces the synthesis of putrescine and that the accumulation of putrescines is essential for the induction of MeJA-mediated chilling tolerance of rice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological and biochemical changes related with methyl jasmonate-induced chilling tolerance of rice plants.
the effects of exogenous MeJA on physiological and biochemical changes related with chilling tolerance of rice plants.
the physiological and biochemical changes of rice seedlings in response to MeJA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MeJA-induced chilling tolerance in rice seedlings was closely related to the increase in putrescine level, which was induced by the activation of ADC.
MeJA-induced chilling tolerance in rice is mediated by the accumulation of putrescine and that the accumulation is mediated by the activation of ADC and SAMDC.
the induction of chilling resistance by MeJA is associated with the accumulation of putrescine, and this effect is mediated by ADC.

MeJA-induced putrascine accumulation is required to improve the survival ratio of rice seedlings exposed to chilling stress.
